The company's rules for taking in a TOC

Source: R/toc_rules.R
toc_rules.Rd

A company keeps one rule set or several for its TOCs, in the company standards workbook (company_standards()): the sheet toc_map (an item's candidate column names, | between them, by rule_set; blank is standard) and the sheet toc_rules (a row a set: its sheet names, header rows, phases, suffixes, Topline flag, shell sheet names, how the output id is made; a blank takes the default). A workbook written before either reads as one set, standard, with the defaults.

Usage

toc_rules(home = tflplanner_home(), standards = NULL)

toc_rule_set(rules, name = NULL, overrides = NULL)

toc_map_for(headers, std = company_standards()$toc_map, rule_set = NULL)

toc_pick_rules(headers, rules)

Arguments

home

tflplanner's home.

standards

The company standards (a list of sheets); by default those in use.

rules

What toc_rules() returned.

name

A rule set's name.

overrides

Settings a study changes (its profile): a named list (number_suffix, title_suffix, title_line, ...).

headers

A TOC's column names.

std

A rule set, what toc_rules() returned, or the standards' toc_map sheet.

rule_set

The rule set's name (std a list of sets or the toc_map sheet); by default standard.

Value

toc_rules(): a named list of toc_rule_sets (name, label, settings, map: item, columns).

toc_rule_set(): a toc_rule_set.

toc_map_for(): a named list, item -> the TOC's column (an item: the first of its candidates the TOC has; title and footnote: every one, in the TOC's order); attr(, "missing"): the items the set names that the TOC has no column for.

toc_pick_rules(): a data frame, the best set first: rule_set, label, required_ok, matched (items with a column), named (items the set names), items.

Details

  • toc_rules(): every rule set, its settings with the defaults filled.

  • toc_rule_set(): one, by name.

  • toc_pick_rules(): the sets scored on a TOC's column names: a set whose title item has no column is out; the most items matched wins, then the set's order.

  • toc_map_for(): which of a TOC's columns is what, by a rule set.

Examples

r <- toc_rules(home = tempfile())
names(r)
#> [1] "standard"  "two-phase"
toc_pick_rules(c("Shell Number", "Title1", "Title2", "g-", "Topline"), r)
#>    rule_set      label required_ok matched named
#> 1 two-phase Two phases        TRUE       4    17
#> 2  standard   Standard       FALSE       1    11
#>                              items
#> 1 output_id, title, phase, topline
#> 2                            title
